text.p: The San Francisco Giants broke out to a 6-0 lead in the first inning, sparked by Damon Berryhill's three-run homer, but manager Dusty Baker said the key to their 8-6 victory over the Montreal Expos Sunday was the bullpen.
Despite the 6-0 lead, Wilson Alvarez could not get the win. He lasted 4 1/3 innings and allowed five runs and four hits before leaving with tightness in his left shoulder.
"That was too close for comfort, especially when you jump them with a six-run first inning," said Baker. "We left a lot of runners on and you started wondering if it was going to haunt us later."

Doug Henry (4-4), Julian Tavarez and Roberto Hernandez combined to pitch 3 2/3 scoreless innings for the Giants. Rod Beck worked the ninth and picked up his league-leading 34th save despite yielding an RBI single to Jose Vidro.
"The name of the game was their bullpen and our bullpen," said Baker. "With Henry, Tavarez and Hernandez in succession and then with Beck we have a group that can do the job."
Darryl Hamilton's two-run homer off reliever Jim Bullinger in the eighth gave the Giants an 8-5 lead.
"The two-run homer off Bullinger was the game," said Expos manager Felipe Alou. "We had the feeling we could get to Beck or anyone with a one-run deficit."
"The home run that Hambone (Hamilton) hit was big," said Baker.
Jose Paniagua (0-1), making his first appearance of the season for the Expos, allowed all six runs and five hits in the first before departing.
"He didn't have much life in his fastball," said Alou.
The Expos chipped away at the lead while relievers Anthony Telford, Marc Valdes and Steve Kline threw six scoreless innings. Rondell White and Vladimir Guerrero homered.
The first-place Giants moved 2 1/2 games ahead of the Dodgers in the National League West.
In Los Angeles, Brett Tomko gave up seven hits over seven innings and Willie Greene had a two-run single in the first as the Cincinnati Reds blanked the Dodgers 5-0.
Tomko (8-4) struck out two and walked none. Stan Belinda struck out four over the final two innings.
Hideo Nomo (11-10) yielded five runs and eight hits in seven innings, walking four and striking out 10.
In St Louis, Danny Sheaffer drove in three runs, including a two-run double that snapped an eighth-inning tie and lifted the Cardinals to a 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves.
Denny Neagle (16-3) took the loss. He allowed three runs and seven hits over 7 2/3 innings and suffered his first loss in eight starts since July 6.
Curtis King (2-0) recorded the final two outs in the eighth for the win. Dennis Eckersley struck out two in a perfect ninth for his 29th save.
The Cardinals took two of three games from the Braves after losing their previous six series.
The loss trimmed Atlanta's lead in the National League East to 3 1/2 games over Florida.
At Florida, Moises Alou hit his 100th career homer and collected a season-high five RBI as the Marlins routed the Pittsburgh Pirates 10-2.
Kevin Brown (11-8) allowed two runs and nine hits over eight innings for Florida, which scored three runs each in the first and third innings to stake him to a 6-0 lead.
Steve Cooke (8-12) was bombed in his second straight start, allowing six runs and seven hits in five innings.

At Colorado, Dante Bichette's bases-loaded double keyed a four-run fifth inning and second baseman Eric Young threw out the potential tying run an inning later as the Rockies completed a three-game sweep of the New York Mets, 6-4.
John Thomson (5-7) defeated the Mets for the second time in 11 days, allowing four runs -- three earned -- and seven hits in six innings.
Colorado completed its third straight weekend sweep.
Dave Mlicki (5-10) was tagged for five runs and eight hits in five innings for New York. The Mets have lost seven of their last nine.
In Houston, Derek Bell went 4-for-5 with two doubles, three RBI and two runs scored as the Astros cooled off the Philadelphia Phillies, 11-6.
The Astros, who ended a three-game slide, halted the Phillies' six-game win streak, their longest since June 1995.
Bell is now hitting .364 (20-for-55) with 14 RBI in 13 games when batting second in the order. He also stole two bases to give him 10 for the season.

Phillies starter Garrett Stephenson gave up just one hit through three innings but left due to tightness in his right forearm. Outfielder Gregg Jefferies, who was 2-for-3, left with a strained left hamstring in the seventh.

In San Diego, Mark Clark (10-7) allowed four runs over seven innings to win his second straight start while Mark Grace had two RBI and Doug Glanville collected three hits as the Chicago Cubs edged the Padres 6-5.
Chicago won its third in nine games. The Padres lost their third in nine.
